family_title: Frontier (2025-2026): PEFT for RL and reasoning, amortized adapter generation, adapter merging, diffusion control, continual learning

methods.name: Tina
methods.paper_title: Tina: Tiny Reasoning Models via LoRA
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(r=32, lora_alpha=128, lora_dropout=0.05)  # standard LoRA, trained with GRPO
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A,\ \ r=32,\ \alpha=128;\quad \max_{A,B}\ \mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}\big(\pi_{W_0+\frac{\alpha}{r}BA}\big)\ \text{with verifiable math rewards};\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A,B \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted projection } (r=32)
methods.locus: attention projections (query, key, value, dense) of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B
methods.structure: Plain rank-r LoRA factorization \Delta W = BA; the contribution is the objective: on-policy GRPO / Dr.GRPO reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on a 1.5B distilled reasoning model, instead of SFT.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter is ordinary LoRA, so BA folds into W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (standard LoRA initialization), so RL starts exactly at the distilled base policy.
methods.key_idea: Low-rank RL on a tiny distilled model recovers most of the reasoning gain of full RL at a few dollars per run; the authors attribute this to 'rapid format adaptation': LoRA learns the structure/format that RL rewards while leaving base knowledge intact.
methods.results_note: Best Tina checkpoint reaches 43.33% Pass@1 on AIME24 (>20% reasoning improvement over the base) for about $9 of post-training and evaluation compute.

relations.note: Uses unmodified LoRA as the policy parameterization for RL.
TinyLoRA pushes the same 'RL needs very few parameters' thesis to ~13 trainable parameters.
QeRL is another recipe for cheap LoRA-based RL, adding NVFP4 quantization and noise.

methods.name: QeRL
methods.paper_title: QeRL: Beyond Efficiency -- Quantization-enhanced Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
methods.formula_latex: y = \mathrm{Dequant}(\tilde W_0)\,x + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx,\ \ \mathrm{Dequant}(\tilde W)=S_{\mathrm{FP32}}\cdot(S_{\mathrm{E4M3}}\odot \tilde W)\ (\text{NVFP4, frozen});\ \ \text{AQN: } w_{\mathrm{noise}} = w_{\mathrm{RMSNorm}} + Z,\ Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_k^2 I),\ \sigma_k=\sigma_{\mathrm{start}}\big(\tfrac{\sigma_{\mathrm{end}}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{start}}}\big)^{\frac{k-1}{K-1}};\ A,B \text{ trained by GRPO/DAPO}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted matrix } (r=32 \text{ default})
methods.locus: LoRA on the linear layers of an NVFP4-quantized LLM (Qwen2.5 3B-32B); exploration noise injected through RMSNorm gains
methods.structure: QLoRA-type composite: additive rank-r delta on a frozen 4-bit (NVFP4) base, plus a scheduled channel-wise noise vector added to the RMSNorm scale, which acts as row-wise multiplicative noise on the following weight matrices.
methods.mergeable_reason: BA can be merged into the dequantized weights (giving up the NVFP4 format) or kept as a side adapter; the noise is used only during training.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0, but the starting policy is the quantized base, not the exact bf16 model; noise starts at sigma_start (about 1e-2) and decays over K stages.
methods.key_idea: In RL, quantization noise helps: it raises policy entropy and so aids exploration. QeRL schedules it with Adaptive Quantization Noise and combines it with fast NVFP4 rollouts and LoRA.
methods.results_note: First RL training of a 32B LLM on a single H100-80GB, >1.5x rollout speedup, and Qwen2.5-7B reaching 90.8% GSM8K / 77.4% MATH500, matching full-parameter RL.

relations.note: Frozen low-bit base + LoRA, here with NVFP4 and for RL rather than SFT.
Trainable part is standard LoRA.
Alternative low-cost LoRA-RL recipe.

methods.name: PLoP
methods.paper_title: PLoP: Precise LoRA Placement for Efficient Finetuning of Large Models
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{NFN}(W,x)=\frac{\|W z_{\mathrm{in}}(x)\|}{\|W \tilde z_{\mathrm{in}}\|},\ \tilde z_{\mathrm{in}}\sim\mathcal{N}\ \text{(matched dimension and norm)};\ \ W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \text{ inserted only in module types } m \text{ with the lowest } \overline{\mathrm{NFN}}_m=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D},\,W\in m}\,\mathrm{NFN}(W,x)
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per selected matrix; total depends on the selected module types}
methods.locus: data-dependent subset of module types (e.g. V, O, down-projection), chosen per model and dataset before training
methods.structure: A placement rule that chooses the support (set of module types) of an otherwise standard LoRA, scored by how aligned each frozen W_0 is with its real inputs relative to random inputs of the same norm.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapters placed are ordinary LoRA and merge as usual.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA; the placement is computed from the frozen model before training starts.
methods.key_idea: From infinite-width feature-learning analysis, modules whose weights are least aligned with the fine-tuning data (low normalized feature norm) gain most from adaptation, so LoRA should be placed there instead of a fixed attention or MLP default.
methods.results_note: Beats attention-only and MLP-only placement in SFT and GRPO on Qwen3 (e.g. Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K 63.8% vs 58.6% for attention-only at equal parameter count).

relations.note: Changes only where LoRA is inserted.
Gives a different placement prescription (data-driven NFN versus all layers / MLP-first).
Both allocate adaptation budget across modules, AdaLoRA during training, PLoP before training.

methods.name: LoRI
methods.paper_title: LoRI: Reducing Cross-Task Interference in Multi-Task Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + (B_t\odot M_t)\,A_t,\ \ A_t\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} \text{ frozen random (Kaiming-uniform)},\ B_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ trained},\ M_t=\mathbb{1}\big(|B_t|\ge\tau_t\big),\ \tau_t=\mathrm{Quantile}_s\big(\textstyle\bigcup_{\text{layers}}|B_t|\big);\ \ \text{merge: } W=W_0+\sum_t\alpha_t (B_t\odot M_t)A_t
methods.trainable_params: (1-s)\,r\,d_{out} \text{ (LoRI-S, sparsity } s\approx 0.9\text{)};\ \ r\,d_{out} \text{ (LoRI-D)}
methods.locus: any linear layer (attention and MLP projections of Llama-3-8B / Mistral-7B in the paper)
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through a fixed random r-dimensional projection of the input; only the up-projection is learned, and only on a sparse coordinate mask. Independent random A_t per task give nearly orthogonal row spaces, so merged adapters interfere little.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each task delta is a fixed matrix (B_t odot M_t)A_t, and multi-task merging is a weighted sum, all foldable into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B_t = 0 as in LoRA with A_t random and frozen; masks M_t are computed by magnitude on a calibration run of the dense variant and then kept fixed.
methods.key_idea: LoRA's down-projection can be a frozen random map and its up-projection can be about 90% sparse. Random task-specific projections make adapters nearly orthogonal (easy merging), and sparse masks protect earlier adapters, such as a safety adapter, in continual learning.
methods.results_note: Up to 95% fewer trainable parameters than LoRA while matching or beating it, e.g. LoRI-D reaches 63.2% HumanEval pass@10 vs 50.8% for LoRA on Llama-3-8B.

relations.note: LoRA-FA also freezes a random A; LoRI adds task-specific sparse masks on B.
Restricts both factors of LoRA.
Both rely on frozen random projections to cut parameters.
Reduces merge interference by construction (orthogonal subspaces + sparsity) rather than post hoc.
Alternative fix for cross-task interference when merging LoRAs.

methods.name: SingLoRA
methods.paper_title: SingLoRA: Low Rank Adaptation Using a Single Matrix
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}\,u(t)\,A A^{\top},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},\ u(t)=\min(t/T,1)\ \ (d_{in}=d_{out}=d);\ \ \text{rectangular: } \Delta W=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}u(t)\,A_{[1:d_{out}]}A_{[1:d_{in}]}^{\top},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{\max(d_{in},d_{out})\times r};\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: r\,\max(d_{in},d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer (attention projections in the LLM and Stable Diffusion experiments)
methods.structure: Gram-type update from a single factor: for square W_0, \Delta W = AA^\top is symmetric positive semidefinite of rank at most r; rectangular layers use a row-truncated copy of the same factor. The reparameterization symmetry shrinks from LoRA's GL(r) (B\mapsto BG, A\mapsto G^{-1}A) to O(r) (A\mapsto AQ).
methods.mergeable_reason: AA^T (or its truncated version) is a fixed matrix after training and adds to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Ramp u(0)=0 with Kaiming-initialized A, so the update is zero at step 0 and phased in over T steps (about 1% of training for LLMs).
methods.key_idea: Replacing LoRA's two factors by one matrix and its transpose removes the scale imbalance between factors. The authors prove stable feature learning at infinite width and transformation-invariance of standard optimizers, while halving parameters. For square layers the symmetric-PSD form restricts expressivity, which the paper argues the transformer architecture compensates for.
methods.results_note: Llama-7B on MNLI: 91.3% vs 89.1% (LoRA) and 90.2% (LoRA+) with about 60% of their parameters; DreamBooth DINO 0.151 vs 0.148 (DoRA) and 0.143 (LoRA).

relations.note: Same additive low-rank role with one factor instead of two.
LoRA+ fixes factor imbalance with separate learning rates; SingLoRA removes the second factor.
Both target transformation-invariant optimization of low-rank adapters.
Alternative route to scale-stable LoRA training.

methods.name: T2L
methods.paper_title: Text-to-LoRA: Instant Transformer Adaption
methods.formula_latex: \phi_{m,l}=\big[f(z);\,E[m];\,E[l]\big],\ \ (A_{m,l},B_{m,l})=h_\theta(\phi_{m,l}),\ \ W_{m,l}=W_{0,m,l}+B_{m,l}A_{m,l};\ \ W_0 \text{ and text encoder } f \text{ frozen, hypernetwork } h_\theta \text{ trained by } \min_\theta \mathbb{E}_i\|\Delta W^i-h_\theta(\phi^i)\| \text{ (reconstruction) or the downstream SFT loss}
methods.trainable_params: |\theta| \text{ for the whole model, shared by all tasks: } 4.9\mathrm{M}\ (S),\ 34.3\mathrm{M}\ (M),\ 55.3\mathrm{M}\ (L);\ \text{each generated adapter has } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ entries per module}
methods.locus: query and value projections of every layer (Mistral-7B-Instruct, r = 8); z is a natural-language task description
methods.structure: Amortized adapter: a learned map h_\theta from (task-description embedding x module-type embedding x layer embedding) to rank-r factor pairs, so the reachable adapters form a text-parameterized family inside LoRA space. The deployed modification is additive low-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: Once generated for a given description the LoRA merges into W_0 as usual; the hypernetwork is needed only at adaptation time, one adapter per task.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity guarantee by construction: the generated adapter is generally nonzero for any description. Removing it restores W_0 exactly.
methods.key_idea: Compress many task-specific LoRAs into one hypernetwork conditioned on a natural-language task description, so a new adapter comes from a single forward pass with no data or gradient steps and generalizes zero-shot to unseen tasks.
methods.results_note: SFT-trained T2L on Mistral-7B-Instruct averages 67.7% zero-shot over 10 benchmarks vs 66.3% for a multi-task LoRA, and reconstruction-trained T2L nearly matches the task-specific LoRAs it compresses.

relations.note: Hypernetwork-generated adapters conditioned on task information, here emitting LoRA factors from text.
The output object is a LoRA adapter.
DnD conditions on unlabeled task prompts instead of a task description.

methods.name: DnD
methods.paper_title: Drag-and-Drop LLMs: Zero-Shot Prompt-to-Weights
methods.formula_latex: c=\mathrm{Enc}\big(\{p_1,\dots,p_N\}\big)\ (\text{frozen Sentence-BERT, unlabeled prompts}),\ \ \widehat{\Theta}=\mathcal{D}_\theta(c)\ (\text{hyper-convolutional decoder}),\ \ W=W_0+\widehat{B}\widehat{A};\ \ \min_\theta\ \big\|\mathcal{D}_\theta(c)-\mathrm{tok}(\Theta_{\mathrm{LoRA}})\big\|_2^2
methods.trainable_params: |\theta| \text{ (decoder, shared across tasks); each generated adapter has } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ entries per adapted matrix}
methods.locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices in all layers (Qwen2.5 0.5B-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B)
methods.structure: Generator from a batch of unlabeled task prompts to the full set of tokenized LoRA weights, trained on prompt-checkpoint pairs collected along LoRA fine-tuning trajectories. The deployed modification is additive low-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: A generated adapter merges into W_0 like any LoRA; the generator is only used at adaptation time.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity guarantee: the decoder emits a nonzero adapter; removing it restores W_0.
methods.key_idea: Treat adaptation as conditional weight generation: map a handful of unlabeled prompts from a new task straight to LoRA weights in seconds, skipping per-task training.
methods.results_note: Generates adapters in under a second (up to 12,000x lower overhead than fine-tuning) with average gains up to 30% over the training LoRAs on unseen commonsense, math, coding and multimodal benchmarks.

relations.note: Both are prompt/text-conditioned LoRA generators; DnD uses unlabeled prompt batches and a convolutional decoder.
Generated object is a LoRA adapter.

methods.name: D2L
methods.paper_title: Doc-to-LoRA: Learning to Instantly Internalize Contexts
methods.formula_latex: (A_l^{(k)},B_l^{(k)})=H_\phi\big(\text{activations of chunk } c^{(k)} \text{ in the frozen LLM}\big)_l,\ \ W_l'=W_l+\alpha_l\,[B_l^{(1)}\cdots B_l^{(K)}]\,[A_l^{(1)};\dots;A_l^{(K)}];\ \ \min_\phi\ \mathbb{E}_{c,(x,y)}\,\mathrm{KL}\big(p_\theta(y\mid x,c)\,\|\,p_{\theta+H_\phi(c)}(y\mid x)\big)
methods.trainable_params: |\phi| \text{ (Perceiver hypernetwork, meta-trained once); generated adapter } K r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per MLP down-projection for a } K\text{-chunk document } (r=8)
methods.locus: MLP down-projection of every layer (Gemma-2-2B-IT)
methods.structure: Context distillation amortized into a hypernetwork: Perceiver cross-attention over per-layer document activations emits rank-8 factors. Long documents are chunked and per-chunk adapters are concatenated along the rank axis, so \Delta W=\sum_k B^{(k)}A^{(k)} (adapters compose additively, rank grows as Kr).
methods.mergeable_reason: The generated adapter for a given document can be merged, but each document has its own adapter, so it is normally kept as a swappable side module.
methods.identity_at_init: Not identity by design; base weights are untouched, so dropping the adapter recovers the base model.
methods.key_idea: Meta-learn approximate context distillation: a hypernetwork reads a document once and emits a LoRA, so later queries are answered without the document in context, cutting latency and KV-cache memory.
methods.results_note: Near-perfect zero-shot needle-in-a-haystack accuracy at more than 4x the target model's native context window, with sub-second internalization and far lower memory than keeping the document in context.

relations.note: Same Sakana hypernetwork line, conditioned on documents instead of task descriptions.
Both map a context to a parameter delta in one forward pass.
Cartridges also stores a document in trainable parameters (a KV prefix), but trains per document by self-study.
Concurrent context-to-LoRA hypernetwork.

methods.name: SHINE
methods.paper_title: SHINE: A Scalable In-Context Hypernetwork for Mapping Context to LoRA in a Single Pass
methods.formula_latex: \mathcal{M}=\mathrm{LLM}_{\theta_0+\Delta_{\mathrm{meta}}}\big([c;\,m_{1:M}]\big)\big|_{\text{last } M \text{ tokens of all } L \text{ layers}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times M\times H},\ \ \{(A_l,B_l)\}_{l}=\mathrm{M2P}_\psi(\mathcal{M}),\ \ W_l=W_{0,l}+B_lA_l;\ \theta_0 \text{ frozen},\ \Delta_{\mathrm{meta}},\,m,\,\psi \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: \text{meta-LoRA (rank 128) + } M=\lceil rD/H\rceil \text{ memory embeddings + 4-layer M2P Transformer (shared); generated adapter has rank } r=8
methods.locus: linear layers of the backbone LLM (generated rank-8 LoRA); D is the summed input and output width per layer
methods.structure: In-context hypernetwork: the frozen LLM itself (with a meta-LoRA and learnable memory tokens) encodes the context into an L x M memory grid, which an axial (row/column) attention Transformer maps jointly to every LoRA factor. The deployed modification is additive low-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: Generated per context; it can be merged for a fixed context but is normally kept as a swappable adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity guarantee for the generated adapter; base weights are untouched.
methods.key_idea: Reuse the LLM as its own hypernetwork encoder so that context-to-LoRA generation scales with the backbone, producing an adapter for an arbitrary context in one pass, pretrained with reconstruction/completion objectives and then instruction-tuned on QA.
methods.results_note: Reports sub-second, training-free context-to-LoRA generation that beats test-time-training baselines such as SEAL on SQuAD-style QA and improves with backbone size, M2P depth and LoRA rank.

relations.note: Both are self-supervised context-to-adapter generators; SHINE generates all layers jointly.
Concurrent context-to-LoRA hypernetwork.
Extends the text-to-adapter hypernetwork idea to arbitrary contexts.
Amortized one-pass alternative to iterative test-time LoRA training.

methods.name: GenerativeAdapter
methods.paper_title: Generative Adapter: Contextualizing Language Models in Parameters with A Single Forward Pass
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_l = A_1\,\mathrm{norm}\big(A_2 H_l^{\top}H_l B_1\big)\,B_2=A_1\,\mathrm{norm}\Big(A_2\big(\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{M} h_m h_m^{\top}\big)B_1\Big)B_2,\ \ \mathrm{norm}(S)=UV^{\top}\ (S=U\Sigma V^{\top});\ \ \text{streaming: } S_t\leftarrow S_{t-1}+A_2H_t^{\top}H_tB_1;\ \text{base LM frozen, generator } (A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2) \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: \text{generator matrices per adapted layer (about 500M total for 7B models, } d_r=1024\text{); generated adapter about 32M parameters}
methods.locus: attention output projections of every layer (Mistral-7B-Instruct, Llama2-7B-Chat)
methods.structure: Bilinear, linear-attention-like map from context hidden states to a parameter delta: the context enters only through its second-moment matrix \sum_m h_m h_m^\top, compressed into a d_r x d_r state that accumulates additively over streamed chunks, then SVD-normalized (singular values reset to 1).
methods.mergeable_reason: A generated delta can be added to W_o for a fixed context, but it is context-specific and regenerated per context.
methods.identity_at_init: Not identity by construction; the base LM is frozen and recovered by dropping the delta.
methods.key_idea: A lightweight generator, trained self-supervised (reconstruction + completion), turns any context into a parameter delta in one forward pass, giving test-time knowledge injection, in-context learning and personalization without fine-tuning or long prompts.
methods.results_note: StreamingQA F1 rises from 19.5 (SFT) to 31.5 for contexts up to 32K tokens; 44.9 average accuracy on 26 MetaICL tasks.

relations.note: Both generate adapters with a forward pass; GenerativeAdapter conditions on raw context rather than task descriptions.
Both put context into parameters; Cartridges trains per document.
Hypernetwork-generated adaptation weights.

methods.name: GOAT
methods.full_name: Great LoRA Mixture-of-Experts (adaptive SVD priors + optimization alignment)
methods.paper_title: Make LoRA Great Again: Boosting LoRA with Adaptive Singular Values and Mixture-of-Experts Optimization Alignment
methods.formula_latex: h=W_{\mathrm{res}}x+\sum_{i=1}^{E} w^{i}(x)\,s\,B^{i}A^{i}x,\ \ w(x)=\mathrm{softmax}\big(\mathrm{TopK}(W_z^{\top}x)\big),\ \ B_0^{i}=\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{s\rho}}\,U_i\Sigma_i^{1/2},\ A_0^{i}=\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{s\rho}}\,\Sigma_i^{1/2}V_i^{\top},\ \ W_{\mathrm{res}}=W_0-\tfrac{s}{E}\sum_{i}B_0^{i}A_0^{i},\ \ s=\sqrt{3n\eta/r}
methods.trainable_params: E\cdot\tfrac{r}{E}(d_{in}+d_{out})+E\,d_{in}=r(d_{in}+d_{out})+E\,d_{in}\ \ (E=8,\ \text{top-}2)
methods.locus: linear layers of ViT-B/32, RoBERTa-large and LLaMA-2-7B (MoE-LoRA in place of a single LoRA)
methods.structure: Mixture of E rank-(r/E) LoRA experts with input-dependent top-k gating; expert i is initialized on the i-th contiguous segment of the SVD of W_0 (segments tile the whole spectrum: U_i\Sigma_iV_i^\top with start index (i-1)\min(d_{in},d_{out})/E), and a closed-form scale s aligns MoE-LoRA gradients with full fine-tuning of an upcycled MoE.
methods.mergeable_reason: Expert weights depend on the input through the router, so no single static matrix reproduces the layer.
methods.identity_at_init: The residual (s/E) sum_i B_0^i A_0^i is subtracted from W_0; the initial layer equals W_0 exactly only when routing weights are uniform (1/E), so identity holds approximately, not pointwise.
methods.key_idea: Give each LoRA expert a different SVD-derived starting subspace spread across the whole spectrum, and derive the scaling factor that makes MoE-LoRA optimization mimic full-parameter MoE fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Across 25 datasets (image classification, GLUE, NLG, commonsense reasoning) GOAT beats LoRA and MoE-LoRA baselines and closes most of the gap to full fine-tuning.

relations.note: Uses SVD of W_0 to initialize adapters, distributed across experts and the whole spectrum.
Both align low-rank updates with full fine-tuning dynamics.
Mixture of adaptation modules.
Learned gating over several LoRA experts.

methods.name: KnOTS
methods.paper_title: Model merging with SVD to tie the Knots
methods.formula_latex: \big[\Delta W^{(1)},\dots,\Delta W^{(T)}\big]=U\Sigma\big[V^{(1)};\dots;V^{(T)}\big]^{\top},\ \ \Delta W^{(t)}=B^{(t)}A^{(t)},\ \ V^{(\mathrm{m})}=\mathcal{M}\big(V^{(1)},\dots,V^{(T)}\big)\ (\text{TIES / DARE / TA}),\ \ W=W_0+U\Sigma V^{(\mathrm{m})\top}
methods.trainable_params: 0 \text{ (training-free merging)}
methods.locus: every LoRA-adapted layer, layer-wise (ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14, Llama-3-8B)
methods.structure: A joint SVD of the concatenated task updates gives a shared left basis U\Sigma; each task is represented by its right factor V^{(t)} in that common basis, and an off-the-shelf merging operator acts on the aligned V's before mapping back.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged update U Sigma V^(m)T is a single static matrix added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free; no new parameters).
methods.key_idea: LoRA updates for different tasks are poorly aligned (low CKA), which breaks merging methods designed for full fine-tunes. Expressing them in a common SVD basis before merging fixes this.
methods.results_note: Up to 4.3% higher normalized accuracy than existing merging methods on 8 ViT-B/32 vision tasks and +2.9% on Llama-3-8B NLI tasks; introduces a joint-task evaluation benchmark.

relations.note: Uses TIES (and DARE / task arithmetic) as the merge operator inside the aligned space.
Can plug DARE into the aligned space.
Core Space achieves lossless alignment in a much smaller Tr x Tr space.

methods.name: Core Space
methods.full_name: Core Space merging of low-rank adapters
methods.paper_title: Accurate and Efficient Low-Rank Model Merging in Core Space
methods.formula_latex: \big[A^{(1)};\dots;A^{(T)}\big]=U_A\Sigma_AV_A^{\top},\ \ \big[B^{(1)},\dots,B^{(T)}\big]=U_B\Sigma_BV_B^{\top},\ \ M^{(t)}=\big(U_B^{\top}B^{(t)}\big)\big(A^{(t)}V_A\big)\in\mathbb{R}^{Tr\times Tr},\ \ W=W_0+U_B\,\mathcal{M}\big(\{M^{(t)}\}_{t}\big)\,V_A^{\top}
methods.trainable_params: 0 \text{ (training-free merging)}
methods.locus: every LoRA-adapted layer (Llama-3-8B, ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14)
methods.structure: All rank-r task updates lie in the span of the union of their factor spaces; shared orthonormal bases of the stacked A's (row space) and concatenated B's (column space) map each update losslessly to a small Tr x Tr core matrix, where any merging operator acts before mapping back.
methods.mergeable_reason: The reconstructed merged update is a single static matrix added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: Merge LoRAs in their joint core space rather than at full size: the projection is provably lossless, aligns the tasks, and costs far less than full-matrix or KnOTS-style SVD merging.
methods.results_note: State-of-the-art merging accuracy on Llama-3-8B NLI and ViT vision benchmarks at a fraction of the compute (reported ~600x speedup on Llama-3-8B relative to full-space alignment).

relations.note: Same alignment-before-merging idea, done in a lossless reduced space.
Off-the-shelf merging operators are applied inside the core space.

methods.name: K-LoRA
methods.paper_title: K-LoRA: Unlocking Training-Free Fusion of Any Subject and Style LoRAs
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W^{l}(t)=\begin{cases}\Delta W_c^{l} & \text{if } S_c^{l}\ \ge\ \gamma\,\mathcal{S}(t)\,S_s^{l}\\ \Delta W_s^{l} & \text{otherwise}\end{cases},\ \ S_\bullet^{l}=\sum_{i\in\mathrm{TopK}(|\Delta W_\bullet^{l}|)}|\Delta W_\bullet^{l}|_i,\ K=r_cr_s,\ \ \mathcal{S}(t)=\alpha\tfrac{t_{\mathrm{now}}}{t_{\mathrm{all}}}+\beta,\ \ \gamma=\frac{\sum_l\sum_i|\Delta W_c^{l}|_i}{\sum_l\sum_j|\Delta W_s^{l}|_j}
methods.trainable_params: 0 \text{ (training-free)}
methods.locus: attention-layer LoRA weights of SDXL and FLUX diffusion models
methods.structure: Layer-wise, timestep-dependent hard selection between two pretrained LoRA deltas (content vs style), decided by comparing their Top-K l1 mass with a time-ramped scale (alpha=1.5, beta=0.5): content dominates early denoising steps, style later ones.
methods.mergeable_reason: At each timestep the selected LoRA per layer can be merged, but the selection changes over timesteps, so no single static merged weight reproduces it.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free; no new parameters).
methods.key_idea: Only the few largest LoRA entries matter, and early denoising steps set content while later ones set style; so at each attention layer use whichever LoRA has more Top-K mass, rescaled over time, with no training.
methods.results_note: Outperforms ZipLoRA and B-LoRA on subject+style fusion (e.g. CLIP score 69.4% vs 64.4% for ZipLoRA) and is preferred in user studies, on SDXL and FLUX.

relations.note: Operates on community LoRAs.
Different training-free answer to combining LoRAs (selection vs aligned merging).

methods.name: OminiControl
methods.full_name: Minimal and Universal Control for Diffusion Transformer
methods.paper_title: OminiControl: Minimal and Universal Control for Diffusion Transformer
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{MMA}\big([X;C_T;C_I]\big)=\mathrm{softmax}\Big(\tfrac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt d}+B(\gamma)\Big)V,\ \ C_I=\mathrm{VAE}(\text{condition image}),\ \ B(\gamma)=\log\gamma \text{ on the } X\leftrightarrow C_I \text{ blocks, } 0 \text{ elsewhere};\ \ W=W_0+BA \text{ (rank 4) in the DiT blocks; } W_0,\ \mathrm{VAE} \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 0.1\% \text{ of FLUX.1 } (\approx 14.5\mathrm{M} \text{ LoRA parameters for 12B})
methods.locus: all FLUX.1 DiT blocks (attention projections and norms matter most) plus condition-image tokens appended to the token sequence
methods.structure: Input augmentation plus low-rank weight update: VAE-encoded condition tokens are concatenated into the multimodal attention sequence (shared RoPE positions for spatially aligned tasks, offset positions for subject-driven tasks), a rank-4 LoRA adapts the shared blocks, and condition strength is a log-gamma attention-bias block.
methods.mergeable_reason: Even if the LoRA is merged, inference must process the extra condition tokens, so the cost differs from the base model.
methods.identity_at_init: LoRA uses B = 0, but appending condition tokens changes attention outputs from the start; gamma = 0 (bias of minus infinity) removes the condition's influence.
methods.key_idea: A DiT can serve as its own condition encoder: pass the condition image through the same VAE and transformer as extra tokens and train only a tiny LoRA, giving one mechanism for both spatial and subject-driven control.
methods.results_note: With about 0.1% extra parameters on FLUX.1 it outperforms ControlNet / T2I-Adapter on spatially aligned control and IP-Adapter on subject-driven generation; releases the Subjects200K dataset.

relations.note: Replaces ControlNet's trainable encoder copy with token concatenation + LoRA.
Alternative lightweight conditioning of diffusion models.
Subject/image-prompt conditioning without a separate image encoder.
The only trainable weights are LoRA.

methods.name: EasyControl
methods.paper_title: EasyControl: Adding Efficient and Flexible Control for Diffusion Transformer
methods.formula_latex: Q_c'=Q_c+B_QA_QZ_c,\ \ K_c'=K_c+B_KA_KZ_c,\ \ V_c'=V_c+B_VA_VZ_c;\ \ Q,K,V \text{ of text and noise tokens computed with frozen } W_0;\ \ \mathrm{Attn}\big([Z_t;Z_n;Z_{c_1};\dots]\big) \text{ under a causal mutual-attention mask}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 15\mathrm{M} \text{ per condition (FLUX.1-dev): } 3r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per block for the condition branch}
methods.locus: Q/K/V projections applied only to condition-image tokens in the FLUX.1-dev DiT
methods.structure: Token-restricted LoRA: the low-rank delta acts only on condition tokens, so the map on text and noise tokens is exactly W_0; conditions interact with generation only through masked attention (separate conditions do not attend to each other), and condition K/V are computed once and cached across denoising steps.
methods.mergeable_reason: The LoRA applies only to condition tokens, so folding it into shared weights would alter text/noise tokens; inference also processes extra condition tokens.
methods.identity_at_init: Condition-branch LoRA starts at B = 0, but the frozen base still attends to condition tokens, so outputs change once a condition is added.
methods.key_idea: Keep the control signal in its own LoRA-adapted token branch so that conditions are plug-and-play, compose zero-shot across condition types, stay compatible with community style LoRAs, and can be KV-cached.
methods.results_note: About 15M parameters per condition; KV caching cuts inference time by 58% (single condition) and 75% (two conditions) while improving controllability over prior FLUX control methods.

relations.note: Same token-concatenation conditioning, with the LoRA restricted to the condition branch.
Lightweight alternative for spatial control.
Structural analogue in LLMs: aLoRA also applies its adapter to only some tokens so the base computation stays intact and cacheable.

methods.name: ICEdit
methods.paper_title: In-Context Edit: Enabling Instructional Image Editing with In-Context Generation in Large Scale Diffusion Transformer
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{Out}(x)=W_0x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\sum_{i=1}^{N}G(x)_i\,B_iA_ix,\ \ G(x)=\mathrm{softmax}\big(\mathrm{TopK}(g(x),k)\big),\ N=4,\ r=32,\ k=1;\ \ \text{input: diptych [source | masked target] with prompt ``\dots on the right, the scene is identical to the left but \{instruction\}''}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 0.2\mathrm{B} \text{ (about 1.7\% of the 12B FLUX.1 Fill): LoRA-MoE experts and router}
methods.locus: LoRA-MoE on the output projections of the multimodal attention blocks of FLUX.1 Fill (inpainting DiT)
methods.structure: In-context input augmentation (an edit is inpainting the right half of a diptych conditioned on the left half) combined with a top-1 routed mixture of four rank-32 LoRA experts.
methods.mergeable_reason: Routing over experts is input-dependent and the diptych doubles the image sequence at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Experts start at B_i = 0; the training-free diptych prompt already produces edits, which the LoRA-MoE then sharpens.
methods.key_idea: Instruction-based editing can be posed as in-context inpainting of a diptych in a large DiT. A small LoRA-MoE trained on 50K pairs (about 0.1% of prior methods' data) is enough, and VLM-guided early filtering of noise seeds improves results at inference.
methods.results_note: Strong results on Emu Edit (CLIP-I 0.907, DINO 0.866) and MagicBrush with about 0.1% of the training data of prior methods.

relations.note: Both use mixtures of LoRA experts with top-k routing.
Both reuse the DiT's own attention over concatenated image tokens for conditioning.
Experts are LoRA modules.

methods.name: SD-LoRA
methods.paper_title: SD-LoRA: Scalable Decoupled Low-Rank Adaptation for Class Incremental Learning
methods.formula_latex: W^{(t)}=W_0+\sum_{k=1}^{t}\alpha_k\,\frac{B_kA_k}{\|B_kA_k\|_F};\ \ \text{during task } t:\ \Big\{\tfrac{B_kA_k}{\|B_kA_k\|_F}\Big\}_{k<t} \text{ frozen},\ \{\alpha_k\}_{k\le t} \text{ and } (B_t,A_t) \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: \text{task } t:\ r_t(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted matrix} + t \text{ magnitudes (shared across projections)}
methods.locus: query and value projections of all ViT blocks (rank 10, reduced for later tasks in SD-LoRA-RR)
methods.structure: Nonnegative combination of frozen unit-Frobenius-norm rank-r directions with trainable magnitudes: each task adds one direction, while the magnitudes of all earlier directions keep being re-weighted. Variants shrink later ranks (RR) or absorb a new direction into old ones by least squares (KD).
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the sum of scaled directions is a single static matrix, and inference needs no task identity or component selection.
methods.identity_at_init: Not identity: magnitudes are initialized to 1 and each direction has unit norm, so a new task starts with a nonzero perturbation (initialization of A_t, B_t is not specified in the paper).
methods.key_idea: Decouple LoRA magnitude from direction in continual learning: freeze old directions but keep re-weighting their magnitudes. Training then follows a low-loss path into a region shared by all tasks, giving rehearsal-free, selection-free inference.
methods.results_note: ImageNet-R (20 tasks) 75.26% vs 69.89% for InfLoRA, and state of the art on ImageNet-A, CIFAR-100 and DomainNet class-incremental benchmarks.

relations.note: Applies magnitude/direction decoupling to a growing set of LoRA components.
Rehearsal-free continual learning with prompts instead of LoRA.
Prompt-pool continual learning baseline.
Alternative PEFT-style continual learning by constraining update subspaces.

methods.name: Sparse Memory Finetuning
methods.full_name: Continual learning via sparse memory-layer finetuning
methods.paper_title: Continual Learning via Sparse Memory Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{Mem}(x)=\Big(\sum_{i\in\mathrm{TopK}(q(x)^{\top}K)}s_i(x)\,V_i\Big)\odot g(x);\ \ \text{update only } \{V_i: i\in\mathcal{T}\},\ \ \mathcal{T}=\text{top-}t \text{ slots by } \frac{c(i)}{\sum_j c(j)}\cdot\log\frac{|\mathcal{B}|+1}{\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\mathbb{1}[c_b(i)>0]+1};\ \text{all other parameters frozen}
methods.trainable_params: t\cdot d \text{ memory values per step } (t=500\text{ to }10^4 \text{ of } 10^6 \text{ slots})
methods.locus: value table of a product-key memory layer that replaces one FFN (layer 12 of 22) in a 1.3B model
methods.structure: Input-dependent sparse coordinate mask over rows of the memory value table, chosen by a TF-IDF score: slot access counts c(i) on the current batch, discounted by how often the slot is used on background pretraining batches B.
methods.mergeable_reason: Updated memory values overwrite the originals in place, so the memory-layer model keeps its architecture and inference cost.
methods.identity_at_init: No new parameters; training starts exactly from the pretrained memory-layer model.
methods.key_idea: Memory layers are sparsely accessed by design; updating only the slots specifically activated by new knowledge (relative to their pretraining usage) learns new facts with much less interference than full fine-tuning or LoRA.
methods.results_note: After learning new TriviaQA facts, NaturalQuestions F1 drops 89% with full fine-tuning and 71% with LoRA but only 11% with sparse memory finetuning, at the same level of new-knowledge acquisition.

relations.note: LoRA is the main forgetting baseline it improves on.
Sparse fine-tuning, but here the sparse support is defined by memory-slot access statistics.
Alternative sparse fine-tuning method.

methods.name: SEAL
methods.paper_title: Self-Adapting Language Models
methods.formula_latex: SE\sim \mathrm{LM}_\theta(\cdot\mid C),\ \ \theta'=\mathrm{SFT}_{\mathrm{LoRA}}(\theta,SE)\ \ (W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA,\ r=64,\ \alpha=128);\ \ \text{outer loop: ReST}^{EM}\ \text{on } r(SE)=\mathbb{1}\big[\mathrm{perf}(\theta',\tau)>\mathrm{perf}(\theta,\tau)\big]
methods.trainable_params: \text{inner: } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted matrix per self-edit } (r=64);\ \text{outer: the self-edit generation policy}
methods.locus: inner LoRA on all attention and MLP projections (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct)
methods.structure: Bi-level: the model writes its own fine-tuning data and hyperparameters ('self-edits'); a LoRA SFT step turns each self-edit into \Delta W = BA; RL (filtered behavior cloning) reinforces self-edits whose induced update improves downstream performance.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each realized update is an ordinary LoRA that can be merged into the weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Each inner LoRA update starts from B = 0.
methods.key_idea: Let the LLM learn, through RL, to generate the training data and optimization directives that best update its own weights, turning LoRA fine-tuning into an action the model can take.
methods.results_note: On SQuAD knowledge incorporation (no-context), accuracy rises from 32.7% to 47.0%, beating synthetic data written by GPT-4.1 (46.3%); ARC few-shot success 72.5% vs 20% without RL. The paper flags catastrophic forgetting under repeated self-edits.

relations.note: Self-edits are realized as LoRA SFT updates.
Context-to-weights via iterative self-generated SFT rather than an amortized generator.
SHINE amortizes the same context-to-weights step in one forward pass.

methods.name: SparseLoRA
methods.paper_title: SparseLoRA: Accelerating LLM Fine-Tuning with Contextual Sparsity
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0\big|_{\mathcal{S}(x)}\,x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx\ \ (\text{training only}),\ \ \mathcal{S}(x)=\mathrm{TopK}\ \text{channels of the cheap proxy } (U_k\Sigma_k^{1/2})(\Sigma_k^{1/2}V_k^{\top})x\ \ \big(U_k\Sigma_kV_k^{\top}=\text{offline rank-}k \text{ SVD of } W_0\big);\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A,B \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ (same as LoRA)}
methods.locus: frozen main branch of attention and MLP projections (deeper layers sparsified more; output tokens and the first ~10% of steps kept dense); LoRA branch stays dense
methods.structure: Standard LoRA update; the forward/backward pass through the frozen W_0 uses input-dependent channel sparsity, predicted by a training-free rank-k SVD sketch of W_0 (activation norms for FFN/VO, query-key norm products for QK).
methods.mergeable_reason: Sparsity is used only during training; the dense LoRA adapter merges into W_0 and inference is unchanged.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA; the sparse frozen branch only approximates W_0 x during training.
methods.key_idea: LoRA saves memory but not compute; predicting per input which channels of the frozen weights matter, with a cheap SVD proxy, lets fine-tuning skip most frozen-branch FLOPs without hurting accuracy.
methods.results_note: Up to 2.2x compute reduction and 1.6x wall-clock speedup over LoRA at matched accuracy on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning, code generation and instruction following (LLaMA-2/3).

relations.note: Adapter is unchanged; only frozen-branch computation is sparsified.
Different axis of LoRA training efficiency (compute sparsity vs weight quantization).

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models
papers.claim: Across 7 RL algorithms (PPO, GRPO, DPO, ...) and 10 LLMs, RL updates only 5-30% of parameters; the updated subnetworks overlap far more than chance across seeds, datasets and algorithms, the sparse updates are nearly full-rank, and fine-tuning only that subnetwork recovers a model nearly identical to full RL fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Shows the RL update is constrained in its support but not in its rank, a different algebraic type of constraint from low rank. This argues for selective/sparse rather than factorized PEFT when classifying what RL post-training actually changes.

papers.title: The Path Not Taken: RLVR Provably Learns Off the Principals
papers.claim: RLVR's apparent sparsity comes from a model-conditioned bias: updates avoid the principal singular directions of the pretrained weights, preserve the spectrum and rotate the principal subspace very little, whereas SFT targets principal weights. A 'three-gate' theory (KL anchor, model geometry, bf16 precision) explains this.
papers.relevance: Predicts which PEFT parameterizations suit RL: principal-subspace initializations (PiSSA-style) conflict with RLVR geometry. Under RL, the spectral position of an adapter's subspace matters as much as its rank.

papers.title: RL's Razor: Why Online Reinforcement Learning Forgets Less
papers.claim: Forgetting is predicted by the forward KL between the fine-tuned and base policy on the new task; on-policy RL is implicitly biased toward KL-minimal solutions among those that solve the task, while SFT can converge arbitrarily far, which is why RL forgets less at equal new-task performance.
papers.relevance: Gives a distributional (KL) rather than parametric measure of how far an adaptation moves, a candidate invariant for comparing PEFT methods. It also helps explain why tiny-parameter adapters suffice for RL.

papers.title: Evaluating Parameter Efficient Methods for RLVR
papers.claim: Benchmarking 12+ PEFT methods under RLVR on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B/7B math reasoning: structural variants (DoRA, AdaLoRA, MiSS) beat standard LoRA, with DoRA even exceeding full fine-tuning on several benchmarks; SVD-informed initializations (PiSSA, MiLoRA) suffer 'spectral collapse'; and extreme compression (VeRA, rank-1) bottlenecks reasoning.
papers.relevance: The first systematic map of the PEFT design space under RL. Its rank-1 result is in tension with the LoRA Without Regret and TinyLoRA findings that a tiny rank or parameter count suffices for RL.

papers.title: How Much Knowledge Can You Pack into a LoRA Adapter without Harming LLM?
papers.claim: Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with LoRA on growing amounts of new facts shows that a mixture of known and new facts works best, but packing in more new knowledge degrades general QA benchmarks, and biased data makes the model regress to a few over-represented answers and become overconfident.
papers.relevance: Quantifies the capacity/interference trade-off of a single low-rank adapter used as a knowledge store, relevant to adapter-as-memory views (Doc-to-LoRA, Cartridges, sparse memory finetuning).

notes: Scope: 2025-2026 PEFT methods with clear uptake, verified via arXiv / OpenReview / proceedings pages and Semantic Scholar metadata (checked 2026-10-01). SEED TRIAGE: Most seeds exist and are already fully catalogued in sibling families, so to avoid duplicate records they are NOT repeated here; the site should tag them as 'frontier': lora-one, gora, lora-sb, kasa (init-rank); hira, randlora, c3a, miss, gralora, abba, shira (shape/hf-peft); delora, oftv2, polar, road, osf, svf=Transformer-Squared (multiplicative); loft, lora-without-regret (lora-core; also a paper in hf-peft); tinylora (TinyLoRA, 'Learning to Reason in 13 Parameters', 2602.04118, in hf-peft as TinyLoraConfig); alora, waveft, cartridges (hf-peft/prompts); lift (selective). Seeds added here: Tina, LoRI, SingLoRA, Text-to-LoRA, Drag-and-Drop LLMs. TAXONOMY SUGGESTIONS: (1) The hypernetwork cluster (text-to-lora, drag-and-drop-llms, doc-to-lora, shine, generative-adapter) is labeled 'hybrid' but deserves its own class, 'amortized adapter generation'. Each is a learned map from a task/context space into LoRA space, i.e. a functor from contexts to adapters, with the deployed edit always additive low-rank. (2) Token-restricted adapters (EasyControl applies LoRA only to condition tokens; aLoRA in hf-peft only after invocation tokens) form a structural pattern that the modification_kind enum cannot express. (3) Merging operators (knots, core-space-merging, k-lora) act on the space of adapters, not on networks. Core Space shows that T rank-r LoRAs embed losslessly in a Tr x Tr core, a natural 'colimit' object for composition. RL FINDINGS IN TENSION: LoRA Without Regret (rank 1 matches full FT in policy-gradient RL) and TinyLoRA (13 parameters reach 91% GSM8K) versus Evaluating-PEFT-for-RLVR (rank-1/VeRA bottleneck; PiSSA/MiLoRA collapse; DoRA best). RL subnetworks: RL updates are sparse but nearly full-rank. Path Not Taken: RLVR avoids principal directions. UNCERTAINTIES: SingLoRA venue is the ICLR 2026 DeLTa workshop (not the main track); Doc-to-LoRA and SHINE are ICML 2026 per the authors' announcements/README; Path Not Taken found only as a NeurIPS 2025 workshop spotlight; Sparse Memory Finetuning was desk-rejected at ICLR 2026 (arXiv only). SparseLoRA's estimator formula and K-LoRA's exact comparison rule are paraphrased from the method sections (medium confidence). DnD's LoRA rank and target modules are not stated in the text I read. SHINE's numeric results were not fully verified, so its results_note is qualitative. GenerativeAdapter, OminiControl and KnOTS first appeared in late 2024 but were published at 2025 venues. EXCLUDED (too new or negligible uptake as of 2026-10-01): NoRA / Normalized LoRA (2608.31036), NB-LoRA (2609.25618), LSPO (2607.27787), Geometry-Preserving Orthonormal Init for RLVR (2606.31813), SaRA (2409.06633), HyperLoRA portrait (2503.16944), PrefixMemory-Tuning / Prefix-Tuning+ (2506.13674), ORAL (2503.24354), TC-LoRA (2510.09561), LoRA-Diffusion trajectory (2608.12328). HF PEFT v0.21.1 (2026-09-29) has no dedicated tuner for any method in this file; Tina uses plain LoraConfig.
